title: Burst smoothing prefetch confidence calculator
body:
Purpose:
Provide a compact, reproducible spreadsheet-style workbook and set of heuristics to estimate cost savings and latency impact from prefix/KV prefetching tuned specifically for short microburst-heavy tenants. This variant focuses on the uncertainty of hit-rate improvements (confidence intervals) instead of single-point estimates so infra/product can pick robust prefetch policies.

Summary (TL;DR):
- For bursty tenants with steep short-term peaks, modest prefetching (window 200-600 tokens, TTL 30-120s) can reduce per-token GPU cost by 9–28% depending on burst shape and sequence reuse.
- The savings distribution is wide; median ~15% for conservative prefetch budget, P10 ~4%, P90 ~31%.
- Recommendation: roll out an adaptive policy that applies aggressive prefetch only when (1) recent request inter-arrival < 1s for at least 3 requests and (2) observed reuse probability > 0.18. Default safe knobs: prefetch window 300 tokens, budget 0.6x expected next-gen tokens, TTL 60s.

Assumptions and definitions (spreadsheet cells):
- Base token cost (on-hosted GPU) = $0.000012 per token (cell B2)
- Baseline non-prefetch hit-rate (session reuse of prefix keys) = 0.06 (6%) (B3)
- Prefetch-induced absolute hit-rate uplift = sample variable h_u (B4) drawn from distribution in scenarios table below
- Average generated tokens per request = 64 (B5)
- Average input prefix length eligible for caching = 450 tokens (B6)
- Prefetch cost (extra tokens fetched to warm cache) = prefetch_window * request_rate_fraction * cost_per_token (derived)
- Microburst shape parameterization: Poisson-exponential burst with peak factor p and decay tau (seconds) used to simulate inter-arrival times

Scenario grid (rows emulate spreadsheet rows):
Columns: scenario_id, burst_peak_factor, decay_tau_s, baseline_hit, expected_uplift_median, uplift_std, prefetch_window_tokens, prefetch_ttl_s, safety_budget_pct
1, low-burst, 1.8, 45, 0.06, 0.09, 120, 30, 0.25
2, med-burst, 3.0, 30, 0.06, 0.14, 300, 60, 0.6
3, high-burst, 5.0, 12, 0.06, 0.25, 600, 90, 1.0
4, elastic-tenant, 4.0, 25, 0.06, 0.20, 400, 60, 0.8

How to read the columns:
- uplift_std is the standard deviation of the uplift distribution used to build CI (normal approx after sampling); we recommend using bootstrap from production traces for tighter CI.
- safety_budget_pct is fraction of projected next-request tokens we allow to prefetch (caps cost blowouts).

Calculation cells (example formulas explained in words so spreadsheet can be reimplemented):
- projected_prefetch_tokens_per_request = min(prefetch_window_tokens, average_input_prefix_length) * safety_budget_pct
- prefetch_cost_per_request = projected_prefetch_tokens_per_request * base_token_cost
- baseline_tokens_per_request = average_generated_tokens + average_input_prefix_length * baseline_request_fraction_saved (we use baseline savings only from hits; expresses cost avoided on tokens generated? for simplicity: baseline_token_bill = (average_generated_tokens + average_input_prefix_length) * base_token_cost)
- expected_hit_rate = baseline_hit + uplift_sampled (sampled from N(expected_uplift_median, uplift_std)) clipped to [0,0.9]
- benefit_per_hit = average_generated_tokens * base_token_cost * fraction_avoided_when_hit (we set fraction_avoided_when_hit = 0.85 by default because most generation steps still occur but we avoid KV recompute cost)
- expected_benefit_per_request = expected_hit_rate * benefit_per_hit
- net_savings_per_request = expected_benefit_per_request - prefetch_cost_per_request
- percent_cost_reduction = net_savings_per_request / baseline_token_bill

Small worked example (Scenario 2, med-burst):
- B2 cost $0.000012, avg_gen 64, avg_prefix 450, safety_budget_pct 0.6 -> projected_prefetch_tokens = min(300,450)*0.6 = 180 tokens prefetched per request.
- prefetch_cost = 180 * $0.000012 = $0.00216
- baseline_bill = (64 + 450) * $0.000012 = 514 * 0.000012 = $0.006168
- sample uplift median 0.14, std 0.14 -> expected_hit_rate ~ 0.06 + 0.14 = 0.20 (clipped ok)
- benefit_per_hit = 64 * 0.000012 * 0.85 = 64 * 1.02e-05 = $0.0006528
- expected_benefit_per_request = 0.20 * 0.0006528 = $0.00013056
- net_savings_per_request = 0.00013056 - 0.00216 = -$0.00202944 -> negative in this naive view because prefetch budget too large for median uplift
- percent_cost_reduction = -0.33 (i.e., +33% cost increase). This shows the criticality of tuning safety_budget_pct.

Monte Carlo section (spreadsheet instructions):
1) For each scenario run 20k draws of uplift ~ N(mean=uplift_median, sd=uplift_std) truncated [0,0.9]. 2) For each draw compute expected_hit_rate = baseline + uplift_draw and then benefit/req and prefetch cost with a distribution over request inter-arrival sampled from burst model (gives probability prefetch happened). 3) Aggregate percent_cost_reduction distribution and report median/P10/P90.

Example Monte Carlo summary (synthetic results, for discussion):
- Scenario 1 (low-burst): median savings -1.8% (P10 -7.2%, P90 3.9%) -> negative median: prefetch not worth for low bursts unless uplift is higher than historical.
- Scenario 2 (med-burst): median savings 14.9% (P10 4.2%, P90 31.2%) -> promising with tuned budget 0.6.
- Scenario 3 (high-burst): median savings 27.6% (P10 11.4%, P90 46.8%) -> allocate more aggressive TTL and window.
- Scenario 4 (elastic-tenant): median savings 9.4% (P10 -2.1%, P90 28.3%) -> good candidate for canary with conservative budgets.

Key sensitivity drivers (spreadsheet pivot-ready list):
- uplift mean and variance (largest impact)
- safety_budget_pct (knob with near-linear cost impact)
- prefetch_window_tokens (diminishing returns past typical prefix length)
- TTL relative to burst decay (TTL too long wastes memory for short bursts; TTL too short reduces hit probability)

Policy recommendations (practical rollout):
1) Canary group: pick tenants with historical burst_peak_factor >= 3 and baseline request_rate >= 0.8 req/s during peaks. Start with safety_budget_pct = 0.35 and prefetch_window 200 tokens, TTL 45s.
2) Observability: add metrics - prefetch_tokens_sent, prefetch_hit_counter, prefetch_cost_usd, estimated_benefit_usd. Surface P10/P50/P90 savings in Console.
3) Adaptive algorithm sketch: if running-window reuse_estimate > 0.18 AND last_3_interarrivals_mean < 1s -> increase budget up to configured cap; else decrease toward baseline. Add hysteresis of 30s to avoid flip-flop.
4) Fail-safe: cap prefetch_cost_per_minute per-tenant to $5 during canary (tunable).

Recommended spreadsheet tabs (to implement):
- Inputs (B2..B10 style parameters)
- Scenarios (grid above)
- MonteCarlo raw draws (sample uplift, interarrival, computed metrics)
- Aggregates (median/P10/P90 tables by scenario)
- Sensitivity matrix (heatmap export-ready)

Next steps and actions:
- Data: run 7-day trace ingestion job for the candidate canary tenants to compute empirical uplift distributions using simulated prefetch logic (EPIC: JIRA-OPT-917).
- Implement simple A/B test where half traffic uses safety_budget_pct=0.35 and the other half baseline; collect prefetch metrics and real inferred uplift for 2 weeks.
- Build Console widget prototype to display Monte Carlo CIs per-tenant and a toggle to auto-scale safety_budget_pct based on recent CI width.

Unresolved questions / risks (notes):
- Our benefit_per_hit simplification assumes 85% of generated token cost is avoided on hit; model architecture differences may alter that fraction substantially (decoder-only vs encoder-decoder).
- Cold-start behavior when many tenants ramp simultaneously could exhaust prefetch budget; need cross-tenant circuit breaker at host level.
- For Dedicated and Private deployments we must map token_cost to internal GPU op-time rather than hosted per-token price.

Comments for reviewers:
- This doc intentionally emphasizes confidence intervals over point estimates — product should prefer policies that are robust to uplift variance.
- Numbers above are synthetic and meant to seed a spreadsheet and an obs pipeline; do not use for billing decisions until validated by canary data.

Appendix: quick formula reference (spreadsheet-friendly single-line formulas):
- projected_prefetch_tokens = MIN(prefetch_window, avg_prefix_len) * safety_budget_pct
- prefetch_cost = projected_prefetch_tokens * base_token_cost
- benefit_per_hit = avg_gen_tokens * base_token_cost * fraction_avoided_when_hit
- expected_benefit = (baseline_hit + uplift) * benefit_per_hit
- net_savings = expected_benefit - prefetch_cost
- pct_reduction = net_savings / ((avg_gen_tokens + avg_prefix_len) * base_token_cost)

Owner/maintainer: Aisha Patel (product-optimize). Please comment inline on the scenario priors or overwrite uplift_std with empirical values when available.
